title: GPU saturation fingerprints — summary by cluster & pool (7d)
content:
Overview:
This is a 7-day export of our new 'saturation fingerprint' metrics computed per cluster+pool. The fingerprint combines utilization distribution shape, slice fragmentation, burst-credit consumption, and queueing to give a quick-score (0-100) where higher means more saturated/at-risk. Use this for short-term routing/tiering decisions and to prioritize redistribution work.

Notes to self / quick interpretation:
- Fingerprint_score is heuristic: >70 means sustained pressure and microburst risk, 50-70 means moderate with some headroom, <50 is nominal.
- Entropy_index measures variability of per-slice occupancy (0-1). Higher = more fragmentation across slices (bad).
- We included p50/p95 GPU% to check tail behavior, and avg_queue_ms for immediate latency impact.
- tokens_per_sec is a rough application-facing throughput metric (aggregate across requests in window).

Table (CSV-like):
cluster_id,pool_name,region,fingerprint_score,entropy_index,avg_gpu_pct,p95_gpu_pct,slice_occupancy_pct,burst_credit_used_pct,avg_queue_ms,tokens_per_sec,notes
cl-phi-01,priority,na,82,0.72,76,94,81,68,42,1180,High p95 and slice fragmentation; sustained evening surge Wed-Fri
cl-chi-02,reserved,na,48,0.18,42,61,47,12,8,860,Healthy overall; occasional short spikes from nightly batch
cl-lon-03,spot,eu,63,0.45,59,78,56,34,18,640,Spot pool sees transient preemption events; moderate entropy
cl-sin-02,priority,apac,77,0.66,70,92,78,61,55,1290,Sustained high tail; tokens/sec high for chat workloads, consider small burst-cap bump
cl-fra-01,reserved,eu,39,0.12,31,48,29,5,6,420,Underutilized cluster; candidate for temporary spill-in
cl-nyc-07,shared,na,71,0.51,68,89,65,52,33,1010,Mixed traffic, high queue impact on p95; fragmentation creeping up
cl-syd-01,spot,apac,54,0.33,50,72,52,28,15,520,Spot: ok but high variability around promo windows
cl-chi-04,priority,na,88,0.79,83,97,86,73,78,1420,Severe saturation - hitting burst credits and long queues; urgent mitigation

Aggregate quick stats (7d window):
- Weighted fleet fingerprint median: 64
- Clusters > 75: 4/32 active clusters this week
- Average entropy_index (active clusters): 0.41
- Avg burst_credit_used_pct across priority pools: 47%
- Fleet-wide avg_queue_ms: 21ms (p95 fleet queue 67ms)

Anomalies detected (auto flags):
- cl-chi-04: sustained fingerprint >85 for 36 hours, correlated with a canary rollout (see JIRA-INV-1198). Possible model rollback/incompatible quantization causing slower kernels.
- cl-phi-01: recurring evening microbursts aligned with region-locale usage spike (Wed-Fri 19:00-22:00 local) — consider schedule-aware routing

Recommended immediate actions (short list):
1) Prioritize cl-chi-04 for emergency ops triage: revert last canary, collect perf traces, and enable degraded routing to cl-nyc-07 for 6 hours. Owners: Marco/SRE. (Create JIRA: OPS-CHI-EMERG)
2) Increase small burst-cap reservation on cl-sin-02 for next 72 hours to avoid SLA jeopardy for enterprise customers in APAC. Owner: Capacity team.
3) Move 3 low-priority spot workloads from cl-syd-01 to cl-fra-01 during EU daytime (automation rule candidate). Owner: Batch-scheduler
4) Schedule a slot-consolidation run on cl-phi-01 over maintenance window Sunday 02:00-04:00 to reduce entropy and defragment slices. Owner: infra-ops

Follow-ups / tickets to open or monitor:
- OPS-CHI-EMERG: triage cl-chi-04 (traces + kernel selection logs)
- CAP-APAC-BURST: temporary reservation bump request for cl-sin-02
- JOBMOVE-523: automated rebalancer trial: shift spot jobs from APAC evening windows to underutilized EU clusters

Methodology notes (for reviewers):
- Fingerprint_score = weighted sum: 0.4*p95_gpu_norm + 0.25*entropy_norm + 0.2*burst_credit_norm + 0.15*queue_norm (all normalized 0-100). Tuned on historical incidents (Q4 2025).
- Entropy_index computed from slice occupancy histogram using Shannon entropy normalized by log(N_slices).
- Data source: daily exports from internal dashboard (snapshot every 15m aggregated to 7d window). Script: saturation-extracts/saturation_fingerprint_v2.py (linked above).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we expose fingerprint_score in Console as a heatmap per pool? (Pros: fast operator triage; Cons: risk of teams gaming routing by artificially lowering fingerprints)
- Validate whether quantized LLM variants correlate with higher entropy_index (initial signal from cl-chi-04)
- Add correlation with model size and token_length distribution next run

Quick log of edits (notes):
- 2026-03-25: initial export and quick analysis (Aisha)
- 2026-03-27: added anomaly flags and suggested tickets (Marco)
- 2026-03-29: annotated methodology and added owners for immediate actions (Samira)

Bottom line: we have 3 clusters (cl-chi-04, cl-phi-01, cl-sin-02) that need prioritized mitigation. The fingerprint approach is proving useful to triage cross-metric signal, but we should tune weights and test console UX before rolling it out widely.
